title: Add --shout to greet() and the CLI to upper-case the greeting
spec: Add a shout mode that prints the greeting upper-cased. (1) src/samplecli/greet.py: greet gains a keyword parameter `shout: bool = False`; when true it returns the normal greeting upper-cased (greet('Ada', shout=True) == 'HELLO, ADA!'); when false or omitted, output is unchanged ('Hello, Ada!'). Callers pass it by keyword. (2) src/samplecli/cli.py: main(argv) recognises the literal flag `--shout` in any position; it is removed from the arguments before choosing the name, so the name is the first remaining argument or 'world' if none remain. main passes shout=True to greet when the flag is present, prints the result, and returns 0. No argparse rewrite is required; stdlib only. Do not change behaviour when --shout is absent, add dependencies, or edit tests. Note: adding a parameter to greet() touches the public API listed in factory.yaml owner_approval.required_for.

criteria.text: greet('Ada') without shout still returns 'Hello, Ada!'

out_of_scope: Other CLI flags or a general argparse rewrite
